newsitem.title: CHINA: China charges Taiwan moves closer to independence.
newsitem.headline: China charges Taiwan moves closer to independence.

text.p: China hit out at arch-rival Taiwan on Saturday, warning that a recent conference that decided to dismantle the island's provincial government was another step toward independence and would further damage relations.

The island's National Development Conference last December marked a move "too far down the path of separatism", the Xinhua news agency quoted a spokesman for Beijing's Taiwan Affairs Office as saying.
"This move will surely deteriorate the cross-straits relations," the spokesman said.

Taiwan's ruling Nationalist Party and the main opposition Democratic Progressive Party agreed at the conference to freeze all provincial elections, which effectively overlap central government elections since the island is a single province.
"This signals that the Taiwan authorities are further deviating from the "one China' principle and refusing reunification," the spokesman said.

Both Beijing and Taipei say that Taiwan is a province, but China advocates reunification as soon as possible while Taipei says it wants reunification eventually and under very different terms from those offered by Beijing.

The decisions at the conference could be viewed by China as a push by Taiwan toward independence since elimination of the island's provincial rulers would leave only its central government and further dilute claims Taiwan is a province.

"Separatist forces on Taiwan island tried to deny the fact that Taiwan is a province of China in the name of "constitutional reform," in a move to further cut off contact between Taiwan and its motherland," the Chinese spokesman said.
Taiwan's legal status was as a province of China, he said.

"Any attempt to create "two Chinas', "one China, one Taiwan' or "Taiwan independence' will never be successful," he said in a veiled reference to China's threat to use force to recover Taiwan if the island moves to declare independence.
The spokesman said Beijing wanted to hold talks with Taiwan, but only on condition Taiwan's rulers halt activities regarded as espousing independence and allow direct links with the mainland.

An angry Beijing froze what had been slowly warming talks in June 1995 after Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui made a private visit to the United States, cited by China as evidence that Lee wants independence for Taiwan despite his government's pro-unification stance.

"We have repeatedly emphasised our willingness to exchange views with various parties and people in various circles of Taiwan, on the cross-straits relations and the national reunification," the spokesman said.
Beijing would make more efforts, he said but gave no details.
Taiwan Vice-President Lien Chan on Saturday again blamed Beijing for the impasse in Taiwan-China talks and urged Beijing to end the 19-month stalemate.
